answer:
Sort scores descending and process tied values as a group. Accumulated positives/negatives define ROC points and precision-recall points. ROC AUC uses trapezoids in FPR/TPR space. Trapezoidal PR AUC and average precision are distinct: AP uses precision weighted by recall increments. The function returns all three explicitly and rejects a one-class ROC input instead of inventing a meaningful area.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** ROC uses $TPR=TP/(TP+FN)$ and $FPR=FP/(FP+TN)$; precision is $TP/(TP+FP)$. Threshold sweeps must group equal scores before updating the curve. With rare positives, a modest false-positive rate can imply poor precision, so report PR metrics and operational thresholds as well as ROC-AUC. [3](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://www.evidentlyai.com/classification-metrics/explain-roc-curve) and [2](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.average_precision_score.html).
